_comment: Reviewed exceptions for scripts/verify_route_oracles.mjs. real = genuine street/data geometry (evidence in reason); known-bug = accepted pipeline artifact. Regenerate candidates with --write-whitelist, review in the triage gallery, prune stale entries as fixes land. Rebuilt 2026-07-27 against the BUG set after the shape matcher gained the strand-mean reference, and after that reference showed the WOBBLE residue is genuinely pipeline weave — correcting the blanket real verdicts of PR #36.

entries.reason: WOBBLE devM 9.3 m over a 360 m window. Re-reviewed 2026-07-27 with the chord removed from the shape evidence (corridorFollowsData). Every chord available to the old measure was biased: the reference's own chord over the projected stretch slides wherever the corridor is laterally offset and under-reports, the corridor's chord adds a constant offset that makes a real weave read one-sided, and growing a window on a raw trace is impossible at all (8° over 120 m against P90 jitter of 1.9 m). BUG means pipeline-introduced, so the question asked now is whether the corridor left the data: across this window it tracks a single reference to within 0.0 m (bar 4.4 m, the simplify epsilon) and darts off it and back by at most 0.0 m (bar 6 m = 2 x WOBBLE_SIDE_M). The shape is the data's, not the pipeline's. Power checked against the pre-re-centring pipeline, where the phase sawtooth is real: this rule leaves 15 of 28 WOBBLE findings unexplained there, including every ground-truth carriageway alternation (7.3-10.6 m of dart, about half the 14.2 m P90 carriageway separation). Supersedes the 2026-07-27 verdicts of PR #36 (max chord deviation only, missed two-sidedness), PR #37 (reference required to grow its own window) and PR #38 (projection chord, under-reported here by 1.8-6.2 m).

KINK turn 71 deg, flanks 32 m and 25 m. Re-reviewed 2026-07-27 with a same-stretch matcher (rawCornerSwing). The previous verdict compared the corridor's SINGLE-VERTEX turn against a single raw vertex, which a densely digitised corner can never match: the corridor carries a junction in one vertex while the trace spreads it over several — here the sharpest single raw turn within 25 m is only 36 deg. Measured across the corner's own flanks, the traces swing 68 deg against the corridor's 71 deg (within the 25 deg slack the single-vertex match uses), so the corridor reproduces a corner the street really makes. Power checked against degraded pipelines where corners ARE pipeline-made: 2 findings stay BUG with smoothing off, 6 with re-centring off, 31 with both off.

SELF-CROSS — the corridor polyline properly crosses itself here. Reviewed card-by-card in the triage gallery at 2x zoom on 2026-07-27: the route doubles back through this junction and the digitised trace makes the same double-back, so the crossing follows the service. Kept as known-bug rather than real because the class has no shape matcher to corroborate that reading numerically — the verdict rests on the card alone.
